definitions.gloss: after all, in the end, eventually
definitions.explanation: Used to indicate the final outcome or conclusion after considering everything.

examples.japanese: {結局|けっきょく}、{何|なに}も{変|か}わらなかった。
{結局|けっきょく}のところ、{誰|だれ}も{来|こ}なかった。
examples.notes: 結局のところ = after all, when all is said and done

examples.japanese: いろいろ{考|かんが}えたが、{結局|けっきょく}{行|い}くことにした。
examples.english: I thought about it a lot, but eventually decided to go.

notes:
USAGE: {結局|けっきょく} summarizes a situation by stating the final outcome, often after various attempts or considerations. It can carry a nuance of "despite everything" or resignation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{結局|けっきょく}のところ (after all, in the final analysis)
・{結局|けっきょく}は (in the end)

POSITION: Usually placed at the beginning of a clause or sentence.

CONTRAST:
・{結局|けっきょく} - in the end (summarizing final result)
・{最後|さいご}に - lastly, finally (sequence)
・{結果|けっか} - result (noun, not adverb)
